name: Hand-drawn / Sketch
concept: Element drawn by hand, as a single ladder of roughness. Level 1 is a shippable sketch UI with Excalidraw's discipline (clean chrome, hand-drawn content); each rung adds paper texture, wobble, tilt and less legible handwriting (wireframe, notebook, whiteboard/chalkboard, blueprint, napkin, boiling scribble) until level 8 is unreadable on purpose. A daylight variant moves from notebook to desk lamp to chalkboard with the local clock.

sources.title: Introducing Excalifont (OFL-1.1, licence in font file)
tldraw: Engineering imperfection with draw shapes
Camillo Visini: Simulating hand-drawn motion with SVG filters
Codrops: SVG filter texture with feTurbulence
Jekyll Blueprint theme: CSS grid backgrounds

limits: Element Call / widget / Jitsi iframes only know light/dark: blueprint and chalkboard use dark, the rest light; only the frame is sketched.
Compound icons are inline React SVGs: recolour + filter only; just send/check are swapped for rough.js drawings via masks.
User images/video pixels cannot be redrawn: CSS filters (greyscale, cyanotype) and drawn frames only.
Rough outlines are pre-rendered rough.js SVG masks (deterministic); true per-element random geometry would need runtime JS in a virtualised timeline and is avoided.
SVG filter wobble needs in-document <defs> (enhancer); without the enhancer the variants degrade to static frames.
Ruled-line rhythm breaks on media/code tiles; resynced per tile, not perfect.
Balsamiq publishes no official colours: wireframe palette is an approximation.
Unreadable variant keeps the theme picker readable as an escape hatch (deliberate exception to the theme).
Chat-effects canvas and Avatar.ts data-URL avatars keep Element's colours.
